slides.teacher_cue: Compound words are two complete words joined to make a new word with a new meaning. sunshine = sun + shine (not just shining sun — it is the quality of sunlit weather). football = foot + ball. bedroom = bed + room. birthday = birth + day. Decoding strategy: if a long word looks too hard, look for two smaller words inside it. This works for many multi-syllable words.
slides.expected_response: Students identify the two component words in compound words and use that strategy to decode them.
slides.correction_move: Model: look at sunshine — can you see sun? Can you see shine? Both are words you know. Put them together. Students find hidden words in: sunflower, doorbell, playground, waterfall.
slides.observation_note: Watch for students not recognising the component words when they see them in compound form.

slides.teacher_cue: Say sunshine — sun + shine. Find both words. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say sunshine orally and connect meaning before blending.
slides.correction_move: Model sunshine orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for both component words and CVCe in shine.
